gate_results.notes: Authoritative PlayMode run at validated commit 0f11a9bfad31ef45ccccc80cdaacd3e819fe0636 through run_unity_tests_clean.ps1, filter NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.DoorPassabilityConnectionPlayModeTests: 1 test, 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, runner exit 0, final line VALIDATION PASSED. Counts read from test-results.xml (total="1" passed="1" failed="0" skipped="0"), not the console summary. The bound manifest records commit and post_commit both 0f11a9bfad31ef45ccccc80cdaacd3e819fe0636 and tree and post_tree both 1686a0b7196e58c5fce4665229fd06d39689c37c, clean before and after: the run mutated nothing. The single case, DoorTransitions_PublishEnemyWalkabilityThroughPassabilityOwner (NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.DoorPassabilityConnectionPlayModeTests, a sealed non-partial class so the filter cannot silently select a subset), builds its own test-owned door, DoorEnemyPassability, NavMeshObstacle, floor/wall colliders and a real NavMeshAgent on the project's configured agent type, then drives the real DoorInteractable through BindEnemyPassability, StartInteraction/Tick to Open, the private HandleForwardCrossingTriggerEnter to Locked, TakeDamage(MaxDurability) to Broken, and ResetDoor back to Sealed. After each transition it asserts DoorEnemyPassability.CurrentState, the NavMeshObstacle.carving flag, and that agent.CalculatePath to a point on the far side returns PathComplete only when the door state requires enemy walkability (open or broken) and not when it requires blocking (sealed or locked) -- Sealed=carving/no path, Open=no carving/path, Locked=carving/no path, Broken=no carving/path, reset-to-Sealed=carving/no path again. The test never calls SetDoorState directly, so every navigation result comes from DoorInteractable's own production transitions, exactly what VAL-001 requires.
